harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured secure, persistent inventory log forwarding from node2 to node1. Inventory-tagged records are stored in `/var/log/inventory/node2.log`; unrelated records are excluded. Delivery and data persistence were verified after sequential restarts of both nodes. The OS release and kernel were unchanged, with no package installation or upgrade.
actions_performed: Configured node1 rsyslog to accept TCP/20514 only on its managed address and store node2 inventory messages in a root-only, SELinux-labeled log file.
Restricted firewalld access to node2’s IPv4 address; the collector port is not globally open.
Configured node2 to forward only `inventory` program records with indefinite retry and a persistent named queue.
Kept rsyslog enabled at boot and validated both configurations.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, proving changed boot identities and recovered services, access, configuration, and log delivery.
Retained a protected pre-change firewalld backup at `/root/inventory-rsyslog-rollback/public.xml.prechange` on node1.

evidence.requirement: Central collector configuration and secure exposure
evidence.summary: Configuration validation, managed-address listener, node2-only firewall rule, enforcing SELinux, secure file ownership/context, and final healthy state.
Validated durable forwarding rule, successful intended-identity delivery, established post-restart TCP connection, and zero collector matches for both non-inventory controls.

Healthy baseline and old boot ID, reboot acknowledgement, observed collector outage, changed boot ID, restored listener/firewall/access, preserved data, and exact-once delivery of a record queued during the outage.

Healthy baseline and old boot ID, reboot acknowledgement, observed unavailability, changed boot ID, automatic rsyslog/SSH recovery, valid persisted configuration, re-established connection, and fresh post-restart delivery exactly once.

RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained unchanged; the original rsyslog configuration checksums remained unchanged, SELinux/firewalld/SSH stayed active, and no failed units or rsyslog warnings remained.
